entries.title: US imposes tariffs on dozens of trade partners over 'forced labour' imports
entries.snippet: The tariffs target around 60 trading partners over claims they failed to properly stop forced labour.

entries.title: Oil prices hit $100 for the first time since May
entries.snippet: The price of Brent crude rose more than 6% on Thursday as the war in the Middle East continues to escalate.

entries.title: Indonesian babies were trafficked to Singapore. What happens to them now?
entries.snippet: At least 12 babies have been trafficked from Indonesia to Singapore, but what will happen to them remains unclear.

entries.title: Saudis must recognise Israel for nuclear deal, says Trump
entries.snippet: The US president says the landmark agreement to help Saudis develop nuclear energy is dependent on it joining the Abraham Accords.

entries.title: France evacuates 20,000 as wildfires spread in south-west
entries.snippet: Most of those evacuated were tourists from campsites around Arcachon Bay in France's Gironde region.

entries.title: India activist ends hunger strike after 26 days
entries.snippet: Sonam Wangchuk, a supporter of youth-led protesters demanding education reforms, says he wants to avert "possible violence".

entries.title: Ukraine's ousted defence minister insists on being reinstated
entries.snippet: Mykhailo Fedorov refuses President Zelensky's offer to accept an alternative post, as the battle of wills continues.

entries.title: Teen jailed for exam cheating in Guinea dies after sickle cell complications, father says
entries.snippet: Mamadou Djouma Bah, 17, was arrested and sentenced to prison for exam fraud earlier this month.

entries.title: 'Let's enjoy the ride' says Elon Musk, as AI fears mount
entries.snippet: Talking to The Economist, Musk said he doesn't care if people hate him and said he was not a racist.

entries.title: Nicaragua's legislature debates barring opposition from elections
entries.snippet: The move comes days after President Daniel Ortega demanded 'a wall, a blockade' against opposition parties.

entries.title: Ex-governor convicted of murdering a pregnant student in Kenya
entries.snippet: Okoth Obado was found guilty of killing Sharon Otieno with whom he had had an affair.

entries.title: Blocked by censors, China's animal lovers take fight against abuse offline and overseas
entries.snippet: The killing of a dog and her puppies in Guangdong has sparked outrage inside and outside the country.

entries.title: South Korea woman acquitted of murdering newborn after hospital delivery
entries.snippet: The woman, who had wanted to end her pregnancy at 36 weeks, gave birth to a baby who doctors later killed.

entries.title: Russia's businesses under strain from Ukraine's attacks on Wildberries
entries.snippet: Ukrainian drones have hit several retail warehouses belonging to Russia's biggest online retailer Wildberries in a matter of days.

entries.title: Canada's 'powerful' dairy sector is in Trump's trade crosshairs
entries.snippet: Canada's industry is in the spotlight after the US president singled it out as one of three main irritants used to justify new tariffs.

entries.title: Ghanaians' ICC petition over migrant attacks 'opportunistic', says South Africa
entries.snippet: The petition argues the violence against migrants in South Africa could amount to crimes against humanity.

entries.title: Wreckage of Pan Am plane that shaped aviation safety found 74 years on
entries.snippet: The deaths of 52 people on the Clipper Endeavor led to the introduction of mandatory pre-flight safety briefings.

entries.title: Google and Tesla shares plunge as AI spending rattles markets
entries.snippet: As major tech companies race to capitalize on a new wave of AI technology, investors wonder when financial benefits will appear.

entries.title: Fire kills 10 members of same family in Peru, police say
entries.snippet: Authorities are investigating the cause of the blaze in Lima as local media report it may have been arson.

entries.title: Mamdani backs off pledge to arrest Netanyahu citing lack of authority
entries.snippet: The New York City mayor instead called on US authorities to act on International Criminal Court's arrest warrant against the Israeli prime minister.

entries.title: Trump to impose double-digit tariffs on dozens of countries
entries.snippet: The United States will slap taxes of 10% to 12.5% on imports from 60 countries accounting for 99% of U.S. imports, charging that they have inadequately enforced bans on goods produced by forced labor.

entries.title: How to keep an ancient text interesting to students? Make it a summer blockbuster
entries.snippet: English teachers are excited to have a new adaptation of Homer's The Odyssey to use to get students excited about the epic poem.

entries.title: Egyptian warrior princesses, ancient avocados, and more science news
entries.snippet: Hannah Chin and Nate Rott of NPR's Short Wave podcast talk about the building blocks of birdsong, the evolutionary history of avocados and Egyptian warrior princesses.

entries.title: Trump cuts target federal advisory boards. What does it mean for agencies like NASA?
entries.snippet: The Trump administration has terminated or suspended more than 100 federal advisory committees. Former members say agencies like NASA now have less accountability to stakeholders and the public.

entries.title: Invasive species cause more harm in the Global South
entries.snippet: Invasive species can wreak havoc on ecosystems. A new study in Science suggests low- and middle-income countries in the Global South experience greater harms.

entries.title: Trump allies are poised to weaken protections for historic sites — not just in D.C.
entries.snippet: A council packed with Trump appointees is poised to rewrite historic preservation rules. Critics say that could help him build his D.C. arch faster — and endanger important sites across the country.

entries.title: For a 2nd time, House approves resolution to end the war in Iran in a rebuke to Trump
entries.snippet: Four Republicans joined Democrats to approve the measure. And while it is not legally binding, the resolution represents growing frustration inside Congress over the war.

entries.title: In a first, Chinese woman wins the prestigious Fields Medal
entries.snippet: Despite criticisms of a brain drain from China to the U.S., the awards come at a time when several high-profile Chinese scholars have returned home, some citing an increasingly hostile academic environment in America.

entries.title: Republicans urge Justice Department to investigate former prosecutor Jack Smith
entries.snippet: The former special counsel led two criminal investigations of President Trump and has been a frequent target of Trump's ire on social media.

entries.title: Get into med school in the graphic memoir 'See One, Do One, Teach One'
entries.snippet: Grace Farris' book brings readers behind the med school scenes — documenting anxiety over loans, bouts of impostor syndrome, friendships forged in stress, and the ever-impossible work-life balance.

entries.title: WATCH LIVE: Day 2 of FDA advisory panel meeting to consider use of peptides
entries.snippet: The two-day meeting hosted by the FDA has the backing of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who has described himself as a "big fan" of peptides and vowed to overturn industry restrictions put in place under President Joe Biden.

entries.title: Author Salman Rushdie testifies at terrorism trial of man convicted of stabbing him
entries.snippet: Four years after being stabbed on an amphitheater stage, Salman Rushdie sat across a courtroom from his convicted attacker Thursday and told jurors for a second time about the ambush that nearly killed him.

entries.title: Laura Loomer meets with Ukraine's Zelenskyy after her major reversal on the war
entries.snippet: Laura Loomer, an ardent ally of President Donald Trump with a reputation for incendiary social media commentary, sat down with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Thursday after a dramatic turnaround on the war that could have political reverberations back in Washington.

entries.title: Trump to travel to Michigan ahead of swing state's primary election
entries.snippet: President Donald Trump is set to rally in Michigan next week as early in-person voting begins in the battleground state's primary, where voters will choose nominees for open Senate and governor's races.

entries.title: U.S. military launches 13th night strikes on Iran as clashes escalate over shipping routes

entries.title: OpenAI blamed a hacking event on its AI models going rogue. Here's what to know
entries.snippet: ChatGPT maker OpenAI says it is still investigating the "unprecedented cyber incident" that led its artificial intelligence systems to break out of a testing environment and hack into another AI company.

entries.title: Trump imposes double-digit tariffs on dozens of countries as stopgap 10% levies expire Friday
entries.snippet: President Donald Trump is going ahead with new double-digit tariffs on dozens of U.S. trading partners just as the clock runs out Friday on stopgap levies he imposed after a stinging defeat at the Supreme Court.

entries.title: Earnings at Musk's Tesla fall as spending on research cuts into profit from selling cars
entries.snippet: While the core car business had a solid quarter, Tesla is now focused on building out the infrastructure and AI software that underpins its robotaxis and robotics businesses, which Musk has said are the future of the company. And doing so requires a lot more spending.

entries.title: Thousands are evacuated as wildfire spreads near popular French tourist town
entries.snippet: About 20,000 people were evacuated from towns and vacation resorts along the French Atlantic coast Thursday as the latest in a series of wildfires raged and hundreds of firefighters were dispatched to tackle it.

entries.title: Belarusian opposition leader on fighting for democracy under Lukashenko
entries.snippet: Belarus has been plunged into the center of Russia's conflict with Ukraine, both by its borders and by Putin-linked President Alexander Lukashenko. As the eastern European nation of 9 million grapples with its dictatorial leader and the fallout from the war, Liz Landers spoke to

entries.snippet: At the tip of Cape Cod, a new exhibition is showcasing the work of an artist who spent two summers there in the 1940s. For much of her life, she remained largely unknown in the art world — by her own design. But now, as her paintings receive greater attention, that is beginning t

entries.title: Ben Wikler and Geoff Bennett discuss the Democrats' plan on 'Settle In'
entries.snippet: There's no shortage of analysis about what's wrong with the Democratic Party. Ben Wikler is focused on what Democrats plan to do about it. The former Wisconsin Democratic Party chair wrote "This Is the Plan," laying out lessons from one of the most closely divided states and what

entries.title: Trump administration admits legal errors and withdraws subpoenas of 3 NYT reporters
entries.snippet: Criticized by a federal judge for sloppy legal work, the government on Thursday grudgingly withdrew subpoenas that would have compelled three New York Times reporters to testify about their sources for articles about President Donald Trump's Qatari-gifted Air Force One jet.

entries.title: Police officer's fatal shooting of man with knife roils Madison, Wisconsin
entries.snippet: Protesters burst into a Thursday news conference about the police shooting of a homeless man in Madison, taking the microphone from the police chief and arguing with some attendees who said they wanted to hear more about the investigation.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: US to impose forced labor tariffs on many trading partners
entries.snippet: The Trump administration has unveiled new tariffs on dozens of US trading partners for what it says is lax enforcement of "forced labor" bans. The new tariffs arrive just as a 10% global duty was set to expire.

entries.title: Indian activist Sonam Wangchuk ends hunger strike
entries.snippet: Sonam Wangchuk has ended his hunger strike after 26 days, saying the decision follows a "long negotiation" on various conditions and "in view of possible violence in the country."

entries.title: Trump administration drops New York Times subpoenas over Air Force One reporting
entries.snippet: The White House had targeted journalists from The New York Times for their reporting on security concerns with a Qatari-donated Air Force One plane.

entries.title: Germany seeks energy and trading partners in Africa
entries.snippet: Germany wants to boost relations with Africa. During his trip, German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul has promoted cooperation on energy, infrastructure and the economy. He also criticized US treatment of South Africa.

entries.title: Sweden eases mining permits to cut China minerals reliance
entries.snippet: Sweden has declared the mining of critical minerals and rare earths a national security interest. This will ease and expedite the permit process. The government said the step was needed to counter dependence on China.

entries.title: US threatens 'major military punishment' for Houthi attacks
entries.snippet: President Donald Trump threatened to strike Iran and the Houthi militants over attacks on Saudi tankers. Meanwhile, the UN warned that the situation is 'out of control.' DW has the latest.

entries.title: US-Saudi nuclear deal: How will it impact Middle East, US-Iran war?
entries.snippet: Critics say the US-Saudi deal could spark a nuclear arms race in the Middle East. It's certainly not making US allies, like Israel and the UAE, happy. And reports suggest the US may already be backtracking on the deal.

entries.title: Is Germany investing in the right weapons?
entries.snippet: Germany wants to build up its army and pour hundreds of millions of euros into its defenses. But in a world where the battlefield is increasingly dominated by cheap drones, how many expensive tanks does the country need?

entries.title: US strikes on southern Iran infrastructure widen war
entries.snippet: The latest US strikes on tunnels, bridges and other infrastructure further inland from the Strait of Hormuz could indicate that Washington is shifting gears in Iran.

entries.title: Trump's refugee policy: Only white South Africans welcome?
entries.snippet: Trump is spending more money on refugees, but it's mostly white South Africans who benefit. People from crisis-stricken countries are being denied entry. Experts say the credibility of US refugee aid has been damaged.

entries.title: Man dies of injuries after attack at Regensburg bank: police
entries.snippet: Police say one person has died after sustaining severe injuries at a bank branch in Regensburg. Special units were dispatched and apprehended a suspect armed with a knife.

entries.title: Can India's 'Cockroach' protest movement go nationwide?
entries.snippet: What began as satire on social media has turned into a massive Gen Z-led protest movement driven by anger over corruption and high youth unemployment. There are signs it is finding traction outside of Delhi.

entries.title: Spain's solar eclipse trilogy: spectacle starting August 12
entries.snippet: From August 2026 to January 2028, amateur and pro skywatchers are in for a series of rare solar spectacles over Spain and North Africa. Astronomers expect the events to attract millions from around the world.

entries.title: ECB keeps interest rates unchanged amid Iran war inflation
entries.snippet: The European Central Bank has kept its base interest rates steady but said it was "closely monitoring" the energy price shock. The impact of the war against Iran on energy costs has pushed inflation over ECB targets.

entries.title: Canada-EU: Closer trade ties to counter Trump?
entries.snippet: Given they share the world's longest land border, Canada and the US have historically enjoyed fruitful trade relations. But with Donald Trump escalating his tariff war, Canada is looking to the EU and further afield.

entries.title: Oil prices jump as Hormuz, Red Sea crises deepen
entries.snippet: Renewed strikes on shipping in the Gulf and the Red Sea have dealt a fresh double blow to global oil markets. As prices climb once again, DW examines what else could keep them elevated.

entries.title: WAFCON 2026: What you need to know
entries.snippet: Several months after it was supposed to start and with more teams than first planned, WAFCON 2026 is finally set to begin. The hosts want a maiden title while a tournament outsider have one of its best players.

entries.title: Nigeria: Armed 'bandits' kill more than 20 in Zamfara state
entries.snippet: Armed gangs, known locally as "bandits," are a constant threat in northwestern and central Nigeria. They typically raid villages, steal livestock and kidnap residents for ransom.

entries.title: Czechia: Army helicopter crashes, killing at least one
entries.snippet: A Czech army helicopter carrying five troops crashed in eastern Czech Republic, the military said.
